passage.quote:
Numerical contracts distinguish an ideal calculation over real numbers from
floating-point calculation, which uses finitely many representable values and
rounds results. They bound the resulting error and state the relationship to a
specific PyTorch implementation, rather than assuming the two computations are
identical.

summary: Specify number formats, operation ordering, rounding and permitted approximations explicitly.
Bound the difference between every permitted numerical result and its real-valued target, for both network outputs and weighted output derivatives.
Distinguish numerical accuracy from exact bitwise agreement or agreement within a stated error bound with PyTorch.
remaining: Bit-preserving binary32, nearest-even add/multiply and explicit initial-input range/error proofs support actual scalar forward and separately selected backward kernels, including saved-value recomputation error. General network bounds, other formats and policies, range automation, useful global tolerances and PyTorch correspondence remain unfinished. Exact signaling-versus-quiet NaN realizability remains unresolved.
